sources.entry: TagSpaces - TagSpaces is an offline, cross-platform file manager and organiser that also can function as a note taking app. The WebDAV version of the application can be installed on top of a WebDAV servers such as Nextcloud or ownCloud. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: TagSpaces is a free, open-source desktop app (Windows, Linux, macOS) for organizing, tagging and managing local files offline, with note-taking and a browser Web Clipper.
summary.what_it_does: TagSpaces lets you browse and organize local files and folders, and add tags either into filenames or into sidecar metadata files. Search supports fuzzy matching by name or tag. It includes note creation in TXT, Markdown, or HTML, a built-in HTML editor for to-do lists, and a media player for common audio and video formats. A browser extension (Web Clipper) for Firefox, Edge, and Chrome saves web pages or screenshots as local files. The README says it runs fully offline without cloud services or accounts. The awesome-selfhosted listing describes a WebDAV version that can sit on servers such as Nextcloud or ownCloud, but the README itself does not cover that version.
use_cases: take notes in markdown or txt
manage to-do lists in a file manager
save web pages locally with a browser clipper
search files by tags or fuzzy filename match
how_to_run: git checkout develop # or 'master' for stable release
notable: Tags can be stored directly in filenames or in sidecar files, so metadata stays with the files
Runs a separate Electron utilityProcess worker for search indexing and thumbnails, with no open network port
Includes a Web Clipper browser extension for Firefox, Edge, and Chrome
Has a web version and Android/iOS builds via Capacitor, per the README
caveats: Not optimized for locations with more than 100,000 files
Some features (TagSpaces Pro components in tagspacespro/) are proprietary under a separate EULA
Dual-licensed: commercial license is required for vendors or resellers who want different terms
